notes.meaning: God told Moses to take a small tribute for the Lord from the soldiers' portion of the plunder. They were to give only one out of every five hundred persons or animals. Because the soldiers risked their lives in battle, God required a much smaller share from them than from the people who stayed behind.

The soldiers' tribute was given to Eleazar the high priest as a special offering to the Lord. It helped support the priests and served as a thank-offering for victory. When God gives us success, He asks us to honor Him with what we have received.

The people who stayed in camp had to give a larger portion of one out of every fifty animals and people. This portion was given to the Levites, who took care of the tabernacle. Those at home had not faced danger, and there were far more Levites to support than priests, so God required a larger share from their half.
Moses and Eleazar followed the Lord's instructions exactly. Their prompt obedience showed that Israel fought this war for God's purposes rather than their own greed.

The total plunder remaining from Midian was counted. It included 675,000 sheep, 72,000 cattle, 61,000 donkeys, and 32,000 young women who were not married. These large numbers reflect the great livestock wealth of desert tribes and show the sweeping scale of God's victory.

Half of the total plunder was set aside for the twelve thousand soldiers who fought. From their half, the Lord's tribute was calculated at one out of five hundred: 675 sheep, 72 cattle, 61 donkeys, and 32 people. The captives given to the Lord were assigned to assist the priests in serving at the sanctuary.
Moses handed this dedicated share over to Eleazar the priest as an offering to the Lord. He carried out the command just as the Lord had directed him.

The second half of the spoils belonged to the congregation of Israel who had stayed in the camp. It equaled the soldiers' share: 337,500 sheep, 36,000 cattle, 30,500 donkeys, and 16,000 people. God provided for the entire nation so that all the people shared in the fruits of the victory.

From the people's half, Moses took one out of every fifty animals and persons and gave them to the Levites. The Levites had the duty of caring for the Lord's tent, so these resources supported their daily work. Moses obeyed every detail God gave him.
The army officers, who commanded thousands and hundreds of men, came to Moses. Even though they had returned as victors, they approached him humbly and showed great respect to their leader.

The commanders reported an astonishing fact: after taking a roll call of the entire army, not a single Israelite soldier was missing or killed. This complete safety was an extraordinary miracle. It proved beyond doubt that God Himself had fought for them and watched over every life.

Moved by God's amazing protection, the commanders brought a voluntary gift of gold jewelry, including armbands, rings, and necklaces. They offered it to make atonement for themselves before the Lord. Atonement here means acknowledging their unworthiness, seeking forgiveness for any shortcomings, and thanking God for sparing their lives.

Moses and Eleazar took all the beautifully crafted gold items from the officers. The total weight of the gold was 16,750 shekels, which was an enormous fortune. This remarkable gift showed how eager the leaders were to express sincere gratitude to God.

The common soldiers kept their personal plunder for themselves. While the livestock and captives were divided among the whole community, individual soldiers kept personal items like jewelry without having to hand them over.

Moses and Eleazar brought the gold into the Tent of Meeting as a memorial before the Lord. A memorial was a physical reminder kept in the tabernacle to remember God's faithfulness and Israel's thankfulness. It stood as an ongoing encouragement for the people to trust the Lord in future trials.
